key_insight: Can human forecasters’ written discussions improve tropical cyclone intensity predictions beyond numerical weather data? This study investigates that question across 637 storms; the supplied abstract is incomplete and does not report the findings.
problem_solved: Determining whether National Hurricane Center discussions contain useful predictive information not already captured by numerical environmental and wind predictors.
method: Analyze Tropical Cyclone Discussions for 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific cyclones from the 2002–2023 hurricane seasons.
Combine discussion text with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields.
Assess the added value of discussion text for intensity forecasting beyond the numerical predictors.
impact: The study explores whether expert-written text can complement structured weather data in AI/ML forecasting. It addresses the practical question of whether adding human context provides predictive value beyond existing numerical inputs.
visual_elements: Two input streams—forecaster discussion text and numerical weather data—merging into an intensity prediction.

paper_title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
paper_authors: Ilia Azizi, Frederick Iat-Hin Tam, Marc-Olivier Boldi, Valérie Chavez-Demoulin, Tom Beucler
